root_cause.text: Missing pskb_may_pull() check in skb_gro_receive_list() before calling skb_pull(), allowing a pull from page fragments when skb_headlen is zero, which triggers a BUG_ON in __skb_pull() due to an inconsistent skb len and data_len.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "skb_gro_receive_list() calls skb_pull(skb, skb_gro_offset(skb)) without first ensuring the data is in the linear area via pskb_may_pull(). When the skb arrives via napi_gro_frags(), skb_headlen can be 0 ... hitting BUG_ON(skb->len < skb->data_len) in __skb_pull()." The patch adds the pskb_may_pull() guard and sets NAPI_GRO_CB(skb)->flush = 1 on failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure the skb has enough linear data before using it in GRO receive list to avoid accessing beyond skb data, fixing a potential crash.
intent_record.what: Added a check for pskb_may_pull on skb with skb_gro_offset(skb) before further GRO processing; if it fails, set flush flag and return -ENOMEM.
intent_record.how: Prevents operations on an skb that lacks sufficient linear data, which could lead to out-of-bounds access; instead, the packet is flushed and GRO is aborted with an error.
